oracle_provenance: Welch-Satterthwaite formula, GUM Annex G, standard textbook metrology; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded effective degrees of freedom for a combined uncertainty budget; not a Student's-t coverage-factor lookup itself.

cases.question: With modest per-component degrees of freedom, does the effective degrees of freedom fall in the small-sample regime requiring a Student's-t coverage factor?
With large per-component degrees of freedom, does the effective degrees of freedom exceed 30, correctly indicating the k=2 normal approximation is adequate?
Must a degrees-of-freedom list that does not align one-to-one with the uncertainty-component list be rejected rather than silently mismatched?
With only one uncertainty component, does the effective degrees of freedom reduce exactly to that single component's own declared degrees of freedom, the model's own trivial self-consistency check?
